CNS5.Attribute.innateHint: Innate aptitude modifier. The total beside it includes the averaged base.
CNS5.Settings.attributeRounding.name: Derived attribute rounding
CNS5.Settings.attributeRounding.hint: Agility, Ferocity and Charisma average three other attributes. The rules do not state how to round the average, and every printed example divides evenly. Choose how your table handles the cases that do not.
CNS5.Skill.empty: No skills yet. Add core skills to get the nine every character has, or drag skills in from the C&S Skills compendium.
CNS5.Skill.coreAlreadyPresent: This character already has all nine core skills.
CNS5.Skill.attributesHint: Pick the two attributes the skill is modified by. Choose the same one twice for a doubled attribute, or leave both blank for a competency.
CNS5.Skill.trainingRequired: {skill} cannot be attempted without training. The rulebook marks it [TR].
CNS5.Skill.notOnActor: Personal Skill Factor and Total Success Chance are shown once this skill belongs to a character.
CNS5.Roll.skillTooltip: Roll this skill. Hold shift to skip the modifier prompt.
CNS5.Roll.trainingRequired: {skill} requires training and cannot be attempted without basic knowledge.
CNS5.Roll.modifierHint: Minor ±1-10, moderate ±11-20, major ±21-30, astounding ±31-40, overwhelming ±41-50, catastrophic ±51-75.
CNS5.Roll.critModTooltip: Crit Die modifier from falling outside the Min%/Max% band.
CNS5.Roll.overflowNote: Above Max%, so the Crit Die gains
CNS5.Roll.shortfallNote: Below Min%, so the Crit Die suffers
CNS5.Roll.unskilledNote: Unskilled attempt: a failed Crit Die is worsened by 2.
CNS5.Weapon.skillHint: Matched by name against the character's skills. The weapon takes its success chance from that skill, so raising the skill improves every weapon that uses it.
CNS5.Weapon.skillMissing: This character has no skill by that name.
CNS5.Weapon.noSkill: {weapon} needs the skill "{skill}", which this character does not have.
CNS5.Weapon.rangeHint: Ranges in feet: short, medium, long, extreme, maximum.
CNS5.ArmourLocation.head: Head
CNS5.Armour.empty: No armour yet. Click a piece's name to equip or remove it.
CNS5.Encumbrance.overloaded: Over Carrying Capacity: 1 Fatigue Point per hour for every 20% over.
CNS5.Magick.modeMissing: This character has no skill by that name, so PMF cannot be derived.
CNS5.Spell.methodMissing: This character has no skill in that Method of Magick.
CNS5.Spell.noMethod: {spell} is cast with {method}, which this character does not have.
CNS5.Faith.skillMissing: This character has no Faith skill, so PFF cannot be derived.
CNS5.Faith.pffOverrideHint: Leave blank to derive: half the PSF% in Faith, plus base Spirit.
CNS5.Faith.belowMinimum: This character's Personal Faith Factor is below the minimum for this Act.
CNS5.Faith.tooLowPff: {act} requires a Personal Faith Factor of at least {minimum}.
CNS5.Roll.weaponTooltip: Attack with this weapon. Hold shift to skip the modifier prompt.
CNS5.Roll.spellTooltip: Cast it — you will be asked where the mana is, how far the target stands and what lies between.
CNS5.Settings.strengthDamageSource.name: Strength damage bonus
CNS5.Settings.strengthDamageSource.hint: The rules give this two ways. p106 derives it from the Absolute Strength Rating; p281 gives it as the Strength attribute halved, or quartered for light weapons. The results are close but not identical.
CNS5.Armour.weightModifierHint: Printed weights assume a wearer of 150-174 lb. This modifier is applied once for every 25 lb the wearer is above that band, and subtracted below it.
CNS5.Weapon.apActionHint: Which row of Table - Combat Actions this weapon attacks with. Leave blank to pick one from the weapon's role, group and weight.
CNS5.Weapon.apOverrideHint: Action Point cost is derived from the wielder's PSF% in the combat skill. Set a value here only to override it.
CNS5.TargetArea.head: Head
CNS5.CombatAction.attackNaturalLight: Attack with a natural light weapon
CNS5.CombatAction.attackNaturalMedium: Attack with a natural medium weapon
CNS5.CombatAction.attackNaturalHeavy: Attack with a natural heavy weapon
CNS5.CombatAction.attackHeavy: Attack with a heavy or two-handed weapon
CNS5.CombatAction.drawWeapon: Draw a sheathed light or medium weapon
CNS5.CombatAction.unslingWeapon: Unsling a heavy weapon or shield
CNS5.CombatAction.fireBow: Nock, draw and fire a bow
CNS5.CombatAction.fireBowFast: Nock, draw and fire a bow (fast draw)
CNS5.CombatAction.throwWeapon: Draw and throw a hurled weapon
CNS5.CombatAction.setPolearm: Set a polearm to receive a charge
CNS5.CombatAction.setLance: Set a lance to receive an attack
CNS5.CombatAction.parryHeavy: Parry with a heavy or two-handed weapon
CNS5.CombatAction.blockHeater: Shield block with a target or heater
CNS5.CombatAction.bashHeater: Shield bash with a target or heater
CNS5.CombatAction.blockLargeShield: Shield block with a large shield
CNS5.CombatAction.bashLargeShield: Shield bash with a large shield
CNS5.Faith.vocationsHint: Which vocations may invoke this Act, as printed on pp.145-146.
CNS5.Creation.title: Character Creation
CNS5.Creation.done: {name} is ready. Vocational skills are chosen on the sheet.
CNS5.Creation.overspent: This character is {over} PC Points over budget. Apply anyway?
CNS5.Creation.methodHint: Random and Lion Heart both roll for attributes and differ in how kind the dice are. Design spends a budget of PC Points instead.
CNS5.Creation.designHint: The budget is shown above and updates as you spend. Reserve most of it for attributes.
CNS5.Creation.rollHint: No budget applies to a rolled character. PC Point costs are still shown, for interest.
CNS5.Creation.omensHint: Accept the Neutral default, or choose. Poorly Aspected characters must roll on the Curse table, which is not yet built in.
CNS5.Creation.omensConsequence: Omens set Magick Resistance, decide the aspect bonus to a mage's or priest-mage's Personal Magick Factor, and Well Aspected characters gain extra starting experience.
CNS5.Creation.identityHint: Gender and type together decide the height and build dice at the size step. Race is free text: the human tables are used for anything else, so a non-human character will want its own figures.
CNS5.Creation.backgroundNotice: Steps 5 to 10 of the worksheet — social class, father's vocation, sibling rank, family status, the curse, talents and flaws — are driven by around forty tables across pp.58-101 that are not yet built in. Roll them on paper and record the results here.
CNS5.Creation.notesHint: Anything recorded here is written to the Background & Social tab.
CNS5.Creation.rollAllHint: Random rolls 3d10 and drops the lowest; Lion Heart rolls 2d10. Both add the character type's bonus.
CNS5.Creation.buyHint: One PC Point per level to 15, two per level after that. Humans must buy at least two levels in each.
CNS5.Creation.innateHint: Agility, Ferocity and Charisma average three other attributes. The roll gives a magnitude; whether it helps or hinders is yours to choose, so set the sign by hand.
CNS5.Creation.sizeHint: Roll height and build, or take the average for your type. Height is read straight off the dice as inches; build is adjusted by Agility and Constitution before it decides weight.
CNS5.Creation.weightHint: Weight is ten pounds plus five for every inch over forty, adjusted by build. Editing height or build recomputes it; editing weight directly leaves it alone.
CNS5.Creation.ageHint: The default is eighteen years old with 5,000 experience. Rolling can give more experience at the cost of years, or fewer years and less experience.
CNS5.Creation.reviewHint: These follow from what you have chosen and are recalculated on the sheet, so nothing here needs entering by hand.
CNS5.Creation.addCoreSkillsHint: The nine every character has, plus Accurate Counting for Intellect 12 or better.
CNS5.Creation.nextSteps: Vocational, background and tertiary skills are chosen on the Skills tab, where the compendium can be dragged in.
CNS5.Spell.variableHint: The rulebook prints a word rather than a number here: the cost varies with how hard the caster pushes, or follows the spell's own rules.
CNS5.Spell.rangeHint: The spell tables print one figure and it is the maximum. Short range is a tenth of it and long range a half (p296), so both are worked out from this and from the caster's Magick Level rather than entered.
CNS5.Weapon.noSkillSet: {weapon} has no combat skill set. Open it and name the skill it is used with.
CNS5.Spell.noMethodSet: {spell} names no Method of Magick, and this character knows none to cast it with.
CNS5.Faith.noChanceSet: {act} gives no success chance this system can read. {text}
CNS5.Npc.printedHint: A creature's Body, Fatigue and Action Points are given outright rather than derived from attributes it does not have. Enter them as the bestiary prints them.
CNS5.Npc.modifierNote: Quality and campaign together give this character
CNS5.Weapon.naturalHint: A natural attack carries its own Personal Skill Factor and needs no combat skill.
CNS5.Weapon.psfOverrideHint: Set this for a claw, bite or tusk. It replaces the combat skill entirely: the attack rolls at Difficulty Factor 3 with this as its whole Personal Skill Factor.
CNS5.Skill.psfOverrideHint: A flat Personal Skill Factor, replacing attributes, level and category. The bestiary gives a creature's Dodge, Stamina and Willpower this way.
CNS5.Skill.originHint: Where the skill came from. It carries no bonus of its own — a core or background skill is promoted as a Secondary Skill unless the vocation lists it as Primary.
CNS5.Details.gentleHint: A character of gentle birth gains +10% PSF in Leadership, and in Courtly Love outside the Early Feudal period.
CNS5.Combat.apPoolHint: Action Points for the round: a d10 added to Base Action Points, modified for armour worn, less ten if out of Fatigue.
CNS5.Talent.randomOnlyHint: This ability cannot be bought with PC Points. It can only be come by on the dice.
CNS5.Talent.wrongAspect: This ability is reserved for Well Aspected characters, and this one is not.
CNS5.Flaw.phobiaHint: Facing the phobia calls for a Willpower roll at this penalty. A minor phobia has a 13% chance of proving major, and each major one a further 13% chance of being severe. A character of Ferocity 16 or better may use their FER Attribute Roll instead, and pious laity may take a flat -15% rather than rolling.
CNS5.Flaw.rollsAgain: This result sends you to another table for the detail.
CNS5.Combat.poolRemaining: {name} has {ap} Action Points left this round.
CNS5.Combat.apSpentHint: Take your actions first, then record what they cost. No single action may cost more than {max} Action Points, nor may more than {max} be spent on movement in one phase.
CNS5.Combat.holdHint: Holding over keeps {ap} Action Points for the next round — no more than Base Action Points, which is {bap} — and ends this character's round.
CNS5.Combat.heldOver: {name} holds over {ap} Action Points and is done for the round.
CNS5.Settings.overspend.name: Actions that cannot be paid for
CNS5.Settings.overspend.hint: What happens when a character declares an action costing more Action Points than their pool holds. The rulebook does not settle it, so both readings offered by the game's designers are here. Disallowing is the stricter of the two; allowing lets a character commit to an action and finish it at the start of the next round, before anybody else acts, paying the remainder out of that round's pool.
CNS5.Settings.overspend.disallow: Disallow — no action may be begun that cannot be completed
CNS5.Settings.overspend.finishFirst: Allow — the action is finished first thing next round, and paid for from that pool
CNS5.Combat.disallowHint: An action that cannot be paid for in full may not be begun. Configure Settings offers the other reading, under "Actions that cannot be paid for".
CNS5.Combat.finishFirstHint: An action costing more than the pool holds may be begun. It is finished at the start of the next round, before anybody else acts, and paid for out of that round's pool.
CNS5.Combat.tooMuch: That is {ap} more than the pool holds, and this world does not allow an action to be begun that cannot be paid for in full. The other reading — begin it now and finish it first thing next round — is under Configure Settings, as "Actions that cannot be paid for".
CNS5.Combat.willOwe: That is {ap} more than the pool holds. The action will be finished at the start of the next round, before anybody else acts, and {ap} taken from that pool.
CNS5.Combat.owes: {name} has {ap} Action Points still to pay, and finishes the action before anybody else acts next round.
CNS5.Combat.finishFirstNote: This character has an action to finish from last round, and finishes it before anybody else acts.
CNS5.Settings.defence.name: Combat defences
CNS5.Settings.defence.hint: Basic combat folds the defence into the attacker's chance and rolls once. Advanced combat rolls attack and defence separately and reads them together, which is what lets a shield absorb a blow it stopped and a failed attack hand the defender an advantage.
CNS5.Settings.defence.basic: Basic — one roll, the defence coming off the attacker's chance
CNS5.Settings.defence.advanced: Advanced — separate attack and defence rolls
CNS5.Defence.title: {name} defends
CNS5.Defence.prompt: {name} is attacked. What defence is declared?
CNS5.Defence.none: Nothing warded or worn against magick.
CNS5.Defence.basicHint: An active defence takes half the defender's PSF% off the attacker's chance; a passive one takes a quarter. All active defences cost Fatigue Points but no Action Points.
CNS5.Defence.advancedHint: The defence is rolled separately and read against the attack. All active defences cost Fatigue Points but no Action Points.
CNS5.Exchange.blocked: Turned away — the defending item absorbs it
CNS5.Exchange.reduced: Partly turned — a critical blow met by an ordinary defence still lands, without its Crit Die
CNS5.Exchange.advantage: Missed and met — the defender gains a combat advantage
CNS5.Damage.notYours: You do not have permission to change that character.
CNS5.Roll.fumble: Critical failure — roll Agility to keep hold of the weapon, and the opponent takes a free blow at -20%.
CNS5.Defence.fatigueUnapplied: {name} spends {fp} Fatigue Points defending — apply it yourself, as this client cannot change that character.
CNS5.Roll.asrNote: In a test of strength where both succeed, the lower Absolute Strength wins. This character's is
CNS5.Attribute.asrHint: Strength rolls carry a bonus equal to the Absolute Strength Rating (p106).
CNS5.Settings.critDie.name: Colour the Crit Die differently
CNS5.Settings.critDie.hint: The rules suggest using a different coloured die for the Crit Die, which on a virtual table means recolouring it. Requires Dice So Nice; the Percentile Pair keeps whatever appearance you have chosen for it.
CNS5.Quick.title: Roll against a chance
CNS5.Quick.tooltip: Roll a Percentile Pair and Crit Die against a chance you name
CNS5.Quick.label: What for
CNS5.Quick.noDf: None — roll straight against the chance
CNS5.Quick.dfHint: Naming a Factor applies its Min% and Max% band, turning anything outside it into a Crit Die modifier as a skill check would. Leave it out and the chance stands as typed.
CNS5.Quick.subtitle: Needing {target}% or under
CNS5.Armour.shieldHint: A shield absorbs only when its bearer wins a shield block, so it is not part of what is worn.
CNS5.Armour.coversHint: The parts of the body this protects. A part covered only partly — a hauberk reaches the knees — carries the chance that a blow there meets it.
CNS5.Missile.title: Loosing the {weapon}
CNS5.Missile.rangeHint: Damage and reach belong to the bow and its arrows together, not to either alone, and each bracket carries its own Crit Die modifier. Where a bracket shows a sum, the first figure is the one printed in the rulebook and the second is what a strong arm adds.
CNS5.Missile.strongArm: Strength {strength} tells at a distance: the Crit Die is modified by the missile's own row, and extreme and maximum range reach fifty feet further per point above twelve.
CNS5.Missile.noProfile: {weapon} has no entry in the ranges table, so its reach and damage are unknown.
CNS5.Quick.critModHint: Plenty of things move the Crit Die without touching the chance — a weapon, a range, a spell. A free-form roll cannot know which, so it asks. Anything from naming a Difficulty Factor is added to this.
CNS5.Ammunition.heading: Ammunition
CNS5.Ammunition.none: No arrows, bolts or bullets carried.
CNS5.Ammunition.hint: Loosing a bow asks which of these to load. Damage and reach belong to the launcher and its ammunition together, so they are looked up as a pair rather than added.
CNS5.Ammunition.damageHint: This is what the missile contributes. What a shot actually does is looked up for the launcher and the ammunition together, since the same bow does more with a heavier arrow and reaches less far with it.
CNS5.Weapon.rangesElsewhere: Ranges belong to this weapon and its ammunition together, and are looked up when the shot is made.
CNS5.Missile.assumed: No ammunition of the right sort is carried, so {ammunition} is assumed. Add some to choose.
CNS5.Roll.critOnFailure: The roll failed, so every modifier is applied the other way: a modifier in the character's favour reduces the Crit Die of a failed roll rather than raising it, making the failure less bad (p37).
CNS5.Throw.title: {weapon}
CNS5.Throw.prompt: Is the {weapon} being used in the hand, or thrown?
CNS5.Throw.throwHint: Thrown: {damage} damage, using {skill}, at the ranges the table gives it.
CNS5.Skill.attemptHint: Some skills can be attempted without ever having learnt them, at the Unskilled chance for their Difficulty Factor. Those the rulebook marks [TR] cannot, and are not offered.
CNS5.Skill.noCompendium: The skills compendium is not available.
CNS5.Skill.nothingToAttempt: There is nothing left to attempt untrained: every skill that allows it is already known.
CNS5.Skill.untrainedHint: These roll at the Unskilled chance for their Difficulty Factor, gain nothing for level or category, and worsen the Crit Die by two on a failure. Buying basic knowledge moves a skill into its own category.
CNS5.Skill.categoryOnceLearnt: What this skill will be worth once basic knowledge is bought.
CNS5.Condition.fell: {name} is down at {body} Body, and dies at {deathAt}: {margin} points of life left.
CNS5.Condition.died: {name} is dead, at {body} Body against a Constitution that allowed {deathAt}.
CNS5.Condition.label: Condition
CNS5.Condition.hint: A character is unconscious at nought Body and dead at a negative figure equal to their Constitution (p282), so the margin between falling and dying is their own hardiness.
CNS5.Settings.bruising.name: Wounds beyond a character's Constitution reach the Body
CNS5.Settings.bruising.hint: An optional rule (p281): damage past the armour that exceeds the target's Constitution comes off Body rather than Fatigue, the Body being able to absorb only so much as bruising.
CNS5.Settings.exploding.name: A critical's extra die explodes
CNS5.Settings.exploding.hint: An optional rule (p281): a ten on the extra d10 a Critical Success rolls is re-rolled and added, and again on another ten. This is what makes a lucky blow catastrophic rather than merely bad.
CNS5.Advantage.label: Combat advantage
CNS5.Advantage.attackInTurn: May attack in turn if next in line
CNS5.Advantage.openings: The opponent is off balance: any attack made
CNS5.Advantage.disarmNote: The attacker must make a Strength roll at {penalty}% to keep hold of the weapon.
CNS5.Advantage.restricted: A two-handed weapon or polearm may only counter-attack under the conditions the table gives.
CNS5.Damage.bypassed.critical: A Critical Success takes the whole blow off the Body, so Fatigue absorbs none of it.
CNS5.Damage.bypassed.bruising: More than the target's Constitution got through, so the Body takes it all rather than the Fatigue.
CNS5.Targeting.title: Targeting {spell}
CNS5.Targeting.unknownKind: of no kind the table names
CNS5.Targeting.extend: Extend the range by half again, at double the Fatigue
CNS5.Targeting.dodgeHint: A physical effect may be dodged by a target who is fully alert and at least fifty feet away; their Dodge PSF% comes off the caster. A target closer than that has no time.
CNS5.Targeting.blocked: {obstacle}. No spell passes it, so there is nothing to roll.
CNS5.Casting.scroll: A scroll or book — half Fatigue
CNS5.Spell.rangeUnknown: This range is scaled by something only the Gamemaster can supply:
CNS5.Magnitude.touchSelf: Cast by touch, or upon the caster.
CNS5.Magnitude.sight: As far as the caster can see.
CNS5.Magnitude.engagement: As long as the engagement lasts.
CNS5.Magnitude.fuel: As long as there is fuel.
CNS5.Magnitude.special: As the spell's own description gives it.
CNS5.Save.always: A roll of five or under always resists, whatever the odds.
CNS5.Save.never: A roll of ninety-six or over never resists, whatever the odds.
CNS5.Save.none: This spell allows a save, but the target has no Willpower skill to make one with.
CNS5.Save.casterSkill: The caster's skill in the school
CNS5.Save.label: Save
CNS5.Spell.resistedHint: Left unset, this follows the rule of thumb: spells that charm, command, lure, frighten, hold, confuse, panic or make one hallucinate. Each spell's own description says how it may be resisted, so a Gamemaster may set it either way.
CNS5.Save.hint: These lower what the target needs to throw the spell off, and apply only to a spell that offers a save. Meditation is spent once: the enhancement is a one-shot.
CNS5.Spell.methodPrompt: {spell} belongs to no school in particular. Which Method of Magick is it cast with?
CNS5.Spell.methodHint: A Method is a school — Arcane Magick, Command Magick, Basic Magick – Fire. It is not the same as a Mode of Magick, which is the tradition a mage was trained in, and the casting roll is made against the school.
CNS5.Spell.baseChanceHint: The caster's chance in this school before anything is counted: the target's own resistance, the distance, and whatever stands between them are all settled when the spell is cast.
CNS5.Save.offered: This spell allows its target a save.
CNS5.Magickal.heading: Magickal items
CNS5.Magickal.makerHint: Fixed at the making. The charges an item holds and what a Focus can store follow the Magick Level of the mage who made it, not of whoever carries it now.
CNS5.Focus.hint: A Focus serves only the mage attuned to it. Cast through, it sharpens both skill and aim and lightens the Fatigue: by two for a Simple Focus, by half for a Lesser and to a quarter for a Greater, and never below one.
CNS5.Focus.castHint: Adds to your Method of Magick and your targeting, and lightens the Fatigue.
CNS5.Device.tooMany: More spells than a device of this grade can hold.
CNS5.Device.tooStrong: A spell stronger than a device of this grade can hold.
CNS5.Device.overTotal: More Magick Resistance in all than a device of this grade can hold.
CNS5.Device.makerSkillHint: A Device casts with the skill of the mage who made it, not of whoever carries it: its chance is his Method of Magick TSC%, and a victim's save is measured against his PSF%. That is why anyone can use one.
CNS5.Device.dropHint: Drop a spell here to place it in the device.
CNS5.Device.onlySpells: Only spells can be placed in a device.
CNS5.Device.castSubtitle: Cast with its maker's skill of {maker}%, aimed at {target}% or under
CNS5.Device.castTooltip: Activate this spell. It casts with the maker's skill and costs a charge.
CNS5.Device.materialComponent: Part of the target went into the making (+{bonus}%)
CNS5.Device.noMeditation: Meditation cannot improve a device's aim, nor lower a save against it.
CNS5.Device.removeConfirm: Take {spell} out of {item}? What was recorded of it goes too; drop it back in to restore it.
CNS5.Scroll.hint: A scroll is read once. Its writer's skill casts it, and whether the spell takes hold or not, the wording fades and the scroll crumbles to dust. Reading it needs the language at 65% and a Read Language roll, which is left to the table.
CNS5.Scroll.onlyOne: A scroll holds a single spell.
CNS5.Scroll.wrongGrade: That spell is the wrong strength for a scroll of this grade: Simple scrolls carry MR 1 to 3, Lesser 4 to 7, Greater 8 and over.
CNS5.Scroll.spent: {item} has already been read and has crumbled.
CNS5.Scroll.failed: The spell fails to take shape, so there is nothing to target — and the scroll crumbles all the same.
CNS5.Holds.device: A Simple Device holds one spell of MR 7 or less; a Lesser up to thirteen, totalling MR 21, with none of MR 7 or more; a Greater any number, totalling 21 times its maker's Magick Level.
CNS5.Holds.focus: A Focus stores spells up to a total Magick Resistance of its grade's figure times its maker's Magick Level, and each costs a charge a point of Magick Resistance to cast.
CNS5.Holds.scroll: A scroll holds exactly one spell: Simple scrolls MR 1 to 3, Lesser 4 to 7, Greater 8 and over.
CNS5.Focus.overStore: More Magick Resistance stored than this Focus can hold.
CNS5.Device.failed: The device does not answer, so there is nothing to target — and the charges are spent all the same.
CNS5.Focus.none: No Focus. A mage makes his own, and it serves only him.
CNS5.Focus.sheetHint: Cast your Known Spells through it to add its bonuses and lighten the Fatigue. The spells listed here are the few it stores itself, at a charge a point of Magick Resistance.
CNS5.Scroll.sheetHint: A scroll is read once and crumbles, whether the spell takes hold or not. Crumbled ones are kept here for the record; throw them away when you please.
CNS5.Scroll.castSubtitle: Cast with its writer's skill of {maker}%, aimed at {target}% or under
CNS5.Step.deviceKnown: Known at MR 0, so the device answers without a roll
CNS5.Step.deviceUnknown: Coaxed out at the maker's skill, less 5% a point of MR
CNS5.Step.fromFocus: Drawn from the Focus's own store, without a roll
CNS5.Rate.focus: no Fatigue, being drawn from the Focus's store
CNS5.Book.writtenByHint: Leave blank for your own book. A mage's own book is read to cast spells he is still learning; anyone else's is read like a scroll, at its writer's skill, losing the page of any spell that fails.
CNS5.Book.modeHint: A spell written for one Mode of Magick is useless to another (p306).
CNS5.Book.ownNone: No spell books of your own.
CNS5.Book.otherNone: No one else's spell books carried.
CNS5.Book.ownHint: Reading a spell you are still learning from your own book casts it as though fully learnt, at twice the casting time and half the Fatigue. The spell must be among your Known Spells.
CNS5.Book.otherHint: Read at the writer's skill, like a scroll. A spell that fails to take shape takes its page with it; one that works leaves the book as it was.
CNS5.Book.notLearning: {spell} is in your book but not among your Known Spells. Add it there, however little of it is learnt, to read it from the book.
CNS5.Book.doubleTime: Read from the book: cast as though fully learnt, at twice the usual casting time.
CNS5.Book.failed: The spell fails to take shape, so there is nothing to target — and its page is spent.
CNS5.Holds.book: A spell takes a page for each point of its Magick Resistance.
CNS5.Step.fromBook: Read from your own book, so cast as though fully learnt
CNS5.Step.partlyLearnt: Not yet fully learnt — {remaining} MR to go, so {penalty}%
CNS5.Step.willpowerText: Not born to magick, so the aim is a matter of will
CNS5.Step.corrected: went astray but was caught in time
CNS5.Astray.dispelled: The spell is dispelled without effect ({roll} on Table – Willpower Failure).
CNS5.Astray.near30: The spell strikes the nearest creature within 30 feet of the intended target, or is dispelled if there is none ({roll}).
CNS5.Astray.near10: The spell strikes the nearest creature within 10 feet of the intended target, or is dispelled if there is none ({roll}).
CNS5.Astray.overshoots: The spell overshoots the target by 10 to 30 feet ({roll}).
CNS5.Astray.short: The spell lands 10 to 30 feet short of the target, or less if the caster is close ({roll}).
CNS5.Backfire.subtitle: Not yet fully learnt, needing {need}% or under to cast
CNS5.Backfire.label: Backfire — Crit Die {die}: {severity}
CNS5.Backfire.costs: {fp} FP — {multiple} times the {base} it would have cost
CNS5.Backfire.fizzle: The spell fails, and only half its Fatigue is lost.
CNS5.Backfire.fails: The spell fails, and its full Fatigue is lost.
CNS5.Backfire.major: The spell fails and the Metaphysical Current surges back through the mage: double Fatigue.
CNS5.Backfire.extreme: The spell goes off at the mage's feet, with double Fatigue as the Current surges back. The Gamemaster decides what it does there.
CNS5.Backfire.disastrous: The spell activates in the mage's hand with double its effects, and double Fatigue as the Current surges back through him — a great strain on the heart. The Gamemaster decides what it does.
CNS5.Spell.mrRemainingHint: Nought means the spell is fully learnt, which is where every spell starts. Raise it for one still being learnt: it is then cast at 10% off for each point left, and may backfire.
CNS5.Spell.traditionHint: MR {base} in the table, {modifier} for your tradition (p295), held between 1 and 10.
CNS5.Spell.surchargeHint: {base} FP in the table, plus {extra} because your tradition carries this spell's MR past 10, at 3 FP a point (p294).
CNS5.Details.sunsignCount: The sign grants {count} favoured skill(s), each at +2 levels and +10% PSF, or +20% and a free mastery where the skill is vocational.
CNS5.Skill.favouredCategory: In a category your birth sign favours: it may be taken as a favoured skill.
CNS5.Experience.levelHint: A skill may be raised to this level at its ordinary cost; beyond it, every level of the difference is paid for again. The next level begins at {next} — {needed} to go.
CNS5.Defence.heading: Before the target — {kind}
CNS5.Defence.blocked: {name} turns the spell aside, so the target is never reached.
CNS5.Defence.amuletDischarged: The amulet is overcome, and its own spell discharges for {days} days.
CNS5.Defence.focusBackfired: The Focus fails and turns on its bearer — {roll} against {chance}%.
CNS5.Defence.focusHeld: The Focus fails but does not turn on its bearer — {roll} against {chance}%.
CNS5.Defence.usedDefensivelyHint: A Focus may be held up like an Amulet, resisting by the strongest spell in it. If it fails to stop a spell there is a 20% chance it turns on its bearer (p298).
CNS5.Defence.ageHint: An Amulet or Focus gains 2% of Magick Resistance for every 25 years it has existed.
CNS5.Targeting.meditationHint: An optional rule (p298): +1% per Magick Level a day, or +2% if fasting, up to +25%, stored up in one spell. One spell per Magick Level may be enhanced this way. This is not the meditation below, which is spent on a casting to make it harder to shrug off.
CNS5.Spell.decays: Lasts {duration}, then fades over {minutes} minutes rather than stopping dead.
CNS5.Details.holyStandingHint: Some Acts of Faith are open only to ordained priests, and others also to monastics and members of Holy Fighting Orders (p404).
CNS5.Faith.ordainedOnly: {act} is within the competence of ordained priests alone.
CNS5.Faith.monasticOnly: {act} may be invoked only by ordained priests, monastics and members of Holy Fighting Orders.
CNS5.Faith.needsRecipient: {act} is measured against the one prayed for. Target them first.
CNS5.Faith.automatic: The Act takes effect. It asks no roll.
CNS5.Faith.notGranted: The Act is not granted, and goes no further.
CNS5.Faith.subtitle: Success chance: {chance}
CNS5.Faith.offering: an offering of {offering} from the recipient
CNS5.Faith.costUnread: the cost is given as \u201c{text}\u201d — see the page
CNS5.Spirit.restored: {expended} Spirit expended and all of it restored.
CNS5.Spirit.blessed: {expended} Spirit expended, all restored, and one gained besides.
CNS5.Spirit.shaken: {expended} Spirit expended and only {regained} restored — he wonders whether he has been forsaken ({net}).
CNS5.Spirit.forsaken: {expended} Spirit expended and none of it restored ({net}).
CNS5.Faith.believerHint: What a character's Current Spirit makes of him (p400). It decides who he may pray for, and unlike Body and Fatigue it can rise far above where it began or fall away to nothing.
CNS5.Faith.spiritFromSkillHint: Developing Faith entitles a character to raise his Current Spirit by +1 for every 5% of Personal Skill Factor, rounded up, in the religion he learnt it in (p400). It is his to take, so it is not added for him.
CNS5.Faith.divineAidHint: How many besides himself a character may ask divine aid for (p403). A layman prays for himself; a True Believer may name another instead; from Devout upwards, others in addition. Office counts for far more than belief: an ordained priest reaches ten times his Spirit.
CNS5.Faith.tooManyPrayedFor: {asked} targeted, but a {believer} may pray for {allowed} besides himself (p403).
CNS5.Belief.heading: Congregation & Belief Pool
CNS5.Belief.drawHint: Roll the Belief Pool from the congregation, its building and any shrine. What is drawn stands until it is spent.
CNS5.Belief.hint: A clergyman may call upon the Belief of those worshipping with him rather than spend himself, which is how the costlier Acts are paid for at all. An Act takes from the pool first and from him only for the remainder.
